p: Swansea is a cracking holiday base, with the Gower peninsula's beaches on one side and the city's attractions on the other. But anyone who's spent a week in South Wales knows the weather can change in an instant. That's where an indoor obstacle course earns its keep, giving the kids a proper physical challenge when the beach is off the cards.

Once you're done, there are some lovely indoor and outdoor extras nearby. The National Waterfront Museum in the Maritime Quarter is free and explores Wales's industrial and maritime story with plenty of interactive bits for kids. Plantasia, a tropical glasshouse in the city centre, is warm, leafy and full of plants and creatures from hotter climes, perfect after a grey morning.

If the sun returns, Clyne Gardens near Mumbles is beautiful, especially in spring when the rhododendrons and azaleas are out. Singleton Park is a large green space between the city and the bay, great for a stroll or a picnic. Literature fans may want to look up the Dylan Thomas Centre, celebrating the poet who called Swansea home.
And of course, on a good day, the Gower beaches are hard to beat. Rhossili, Three Cliffs and Caswell are all classics, though the roads can be busy in summer, so set off early.
